datasets.name: bnr-currencies
datasets.title: Currencies with a reference rate of the National Bank of Romania
datasets.description: The currencies for which the National Bank of Romania (BNR) publishes a reference rate against the leu, with the number of units the rate is given for and the first and last day of publication, from 2005. datasets.name: caen
datasets.title: Classification of economic activities in Romania (CAEN), Rev.2 and Rev.3, with the links between them
datasets.description: The sections, divisions, groups and classes of CAEN Rev.2 and CAEN Rev.3, with their names in Romanian, as the National Trade Register Office (ONRC) uses them to decode the activities of companies. A code is unique only within its version and level: Rev.2 and Rev.3 use some of the same codes for other activities, so always read the version with the code. Rev.3 corresponds to NACE Rev.2.1 and Rev.2 to NACE Rev.2. The older versions of the source (1998 and 2003) are not here. The days from which each version applies are not in the source. correspondence.jsonl links each class of Rev.2 to the classes of Rev.3 that take its activities, from the correspondence table of Eurostat between NACE Rev.2 and NACE Rev.2.1: CAEN writes the NACE class codes without the dot. Every class of Rev.2 has a link. Classes of Rev.3 with no class of Rev.2 behind them: 4689.

source.name: National Trade Register Office (ONRC), N_CAEN.CSV and N_VERSIUNE_CAEN.CSV of its newest nomenclatures on data.gov.ro; links from Eurostat, correspondence table NACE Rev.2.1 to NACE Rev.2 (http://data.europa.eu/ux2/nace2.1/NACE2.1_NACE2), published by the Publications Office of the European Union
source.licence: CC BY 4.0, under which ONRC publishes the nomenclatures on data.gov.ro; the correspondence table under the European Commission reuse notice (Decision 2011/833/EU): reuse allowed with the source acknowledged

datasets.update: When INS changes CAEN by order, which happens once in many years

datasets.name: countries
datasets.title: Countries and territories
datasets.description: Countries and territories with their ISO 3166-1 codes, their names in Romanian and English, whether they are a member state of the European Union today, and whether they are in the European Union for VAT, with their VAT prefix. Northern Ireland has the VAT prefix XI but is not a country, so it is not here. Withdrawn entries stay, with their last day of use, so an alpha-2 code can appear on a withdrawn entry and on a current one; the alpha-3 code is unique. Kosovo is not in ISO 3166-1 and is listed with the user-assigned codes XK and XKX. Names are the short names the European Union institutions use, with Romanian letters written with the comma below and without the asterisk the source puts on Kosovo. A name does not state a position on the status of a territory.

source.name: Publications Office of the European Union, Countries and territories authority table; VAT prefixes from the VIES service of the European Commission (https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/rest-api/check-status)
source.licence: European Commission reuse notice (Decision 2011/833/EU): reuse allowed with the source acknowledged

datasets.name: en16931-codes
datasets.title: Code lists of the European standard on e-invoicing, EN 16931
datasets.description: The code lists an invoice under EN 16931 uses, as the European Commission publishes them for the standard: units of measure, currencies, VAT categories and exemption reasons, payment means, document types, electronic address and identifier schemes, allowance and charge reasons, item schemes, reference and text qualifiers, attachment types. They are European, not Romanian; the e-Factura dataset says which codes ANAF accepts. Every archive the Commission still publishes is read, from the one used from 2021-05-17 to the one used from 2026-11-15, so a code that left a list stays with its last day. A code can come back later, as a new row. Names are in English as in the lists. The currencies with a BNR rate are in bnr-currencies, by the same code. The country list of the archives is not here: the countries are in the countries dataset. An invoice writes Kosovo 1A, where countries has XK, and may write XI for Northern Ireland, which countries leaves out.

source.name: European Commission, Registry of supporting artefacts to implement EN16931, genericode archives used from 2021-05-17 to 2026-11-15
source.licence: European Commission reuse notice (Decision 2011/833/EU, CC BY 4.0 for EU content): reuse allowed with the source acknowledged. The codes and their names come from UN/CEFACT, ISO, IANA and the Commission; each file names its origin

datasets.update: The Commission publishes a new archive twice a year, used from 15 May and 15 November

datasets.name: public-holidays
datasets.title: Public holidays of Romania
datasets.description: The days on which no work is done by law, as rules that give the days of any year: a fixed month and day, or a number of days from Orthodox Easter Sunday. Orthodox Easter Sunday is the Julian computus moved to the civil calendar. A day can come from two rules, such as the second day of Pentecost on 1 June. Days declared free by a Government decision for one year only are not included. The two days each of three yearly feasts of other legal religions have no fixed date and are not included.

source.name: Labour Code (Law 53/2003, republished), article 139 (1); Orthodox Easter is computed
source.licence: Romanian legislation, not subject to copyright (Law 8/1996, article 9)

datasets.name: siruta
datasets.title: Administrative-territorial units of Romania (SIRUTA)
datasets.description: The register of administrative-territorial units of Romania kept by the National Institute of Statistics (INS), edition S1 2026: counties and Bucharest, municipalities, towns and communes, and the localities and Bucharest sectors in them, with their SIRUTA codes. Names are in capitals as INS writes them. INS writes them without Romanian letters; the letters come from the copy INS publishes on data.gov.ro, used only where its letters are the INS letters with the marks, and written with the comma below. 4 names keep the INS spelling without the marks, because the two copies spell them differently. The register has no history and no code has left it since 2013. A code is never removed here: if INS drops one, the dataset is not rebuilt until a person decides how it ends. The check digit of the INS methodology does not hold for some codes, so do not reject a code by it.

source.name: National Institute of Statistics (INS), SIRUTA register, edition S1 2026 (https://insse.ro/cms/files/siruta/2026/SIRUTA_S1_2026.rar); names with Romanian letters from the SIRUTA files INS publishes on data.gov.ro
source.licence: CC BY 4.0, under which INS publishes SIRUTA on data.gov.ro (https://data.gov.ro/organization/institutul-national-de-statistica)

datasets.update: INS publishes a new edition twice a year, for the first half and for the whole year

datasets.name: vat-numbers
datasets.title: VAT numbers of European jurisdictions
datasets.description: How a VAT number looks in each European jurisdiction: the prefix, the format in words and as a regular expression, and the name of the tax in the local language. It says which jurisdictions are in the European Union for VAT. A number that fits the pattern is well formed; whether it is registered is a question for VIES or the national register.
